--- title: "PeMS Data Quality" subtitle: "September–October 2022-2025" jupyter: pems-quarto --- ## Monthly Detector Health
2022–2025, September and October — the rest of this report covers 2025 only
Expected station-day intervals is stations × nonholiday weekdays in the month × 288 five-minute intervals per day. Detector health at a given threshold is the share of those expected intervals that were actually observed with `percent_observed` at or above that threshold — the higher the threshold, the less imputed/estimated data is tolerated. ::: {#5cb1ed25 .cell execution_count=2} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

2025 PeMS 5-Minute Interval Data
Before station-days are even assembled, individual five-minute records are dropped when they fail basic sanity checks (missing timestamp/station, non-positive sample counts, or missing traffic-flow values). This section measures that upstream loss directly, out of 25\,297\,920 raw records ingested. ::: {#a030e7e4 .cell execution_count=6} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/cell-7-output-1.png){width=763 height=570 fig-align='center'} ::: ::: The two dominant conditions above, invalid sample counts and missing flow values, overlap: a record can fail both at once. The chart below shows how much each filter catches independently versus together. ::: {#9e90efc1 .cell execution_count=7} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/cell-8-output-1.png){width=667 height=566 fig-align='center'} ::: ::: 508 of 1\,440 stations (35\.3%) have **zero** surviving records after filtering — they are entirely absent from every downstream table. Beyond whether a record is valid, `percent_observed` measures how much of each five-minute reading is actual sensor data versus imputed/estimated. The chart below buckets every raw record (valid or not) by this value. No filter on `percent_observed` was adopted as previous filters already addressed most cases (see below). ::: {#fba7fcf7 .cell execution_count=8} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/cell-9-output-1.png){width=667 height=566 fig-align='center'} ::: ::: ## Overview on Station-Day Pairs
2025 PeMS Aggregated at Station-Day Level
After dropping invalid records, due to sample = 0 or total flow is null
This table summarizes completeness after filtering invalid records discussed above. | Measure | Value | |---|---:| | Station-days evaluated | 36\,217 | | Station-days passing QC | 31\,926 | | Station-days failing QC | 4\,291 | | QC pass rate | 88\.2% | ## Completeness by Time Period
2025 PeMS
The chart below shows the number of station-days that do not contain the expected number of five-minute observations in each model time period. These are dropped in gold layer. ::: {#8b0e12e5 .cell execution_count=9} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/cell-10-output-1.png){width=664 height=566 fig-align='center'} ::: ::: Incompleteness isn't all-or-nothing: the chart below buckets every station-day by what share of its 288 expected five-minute intervals were actually present. Only \-87\.2% were dropped in this process. ::: {#756689a7 .cell execution_count=10} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/cell-11-output-1.png){width=665 height=566 fig-align='center'} ::: ::: Over that same population, the chart below buckets station-days by their *average* `percent_observed` — "100" means fully observed all day with no imputation; lower buckets rely on increasing amounts of estimated values. ::: {#4c6369be .cell execution_count=11} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/cell-12-output-1.png){width=665 height=566 fig-align='center'} ::: ::: ## Completeness Criteria A station-day currently passes QA/QC when all expected five-minute observations are present. | Time period | Expected observations | |---|---:| | EA | 36 | | AM | 36 | | MD | 78 | | PM | 42 | | EV | 96 | | Full service day | 288 | The service day is defined from **3:00 AM to 3:00 AM** the following day.
